properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two faces: committed test key material PEM-encrypted with AES-256-CBC (DEK-Info in test/tls/ca/server.key and test/tls/client/client.key), and legacy CBC suites genuinely configured in a test-only tls.Config in tls_test.go (tls.Listen test server exercising the httputil TLS client). All test fixtures, not production posture, but real crypto artifacts shipped in the repo.

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.24.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production half: base.go:78 is the deployed proxy template — ssl_ciphers ECDH+AES256:ECDH+AES128 permits only ECDHE key agreement (ADH/AECDH excluded), so all recorded TLS traffic through this proxy is harvest-now-decrypt-later. Test half: ECDHE suites in the test-only Go cipher list. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 arm of the production nginx cipher list (ECDH+AES128 in base.go:78, after the preferred AES256 arm) plus AES-128 suites in the test-only Go cipher list. Quantum-safe in practice, below the CNSA 2.0 AES-256 floor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AEAD suites in the test-only cipher list exercising the httputil TLS client; PQ-safe symmetric at the AES-128 floor. Test fixture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 in four roles: production nginx first preference (base.go:78); AES-256-CBC PEM encryption of the committed test keys and the openssl rsa -aes256 -traditional script that writes them; AES-256-CBC suites in the test cipher list; and x509.EncryptPEMBlock(PEMCipherAES256) wrapping a generated RSA-4096 test key (tls_test.go:94, AST-resolved from rsa.GenerateKey at :43). 256-bit symmetric — strongest arm of this repo's posture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Certificate-path infrastructure: production tls.go builds the client trust pool (AppendCertsFromPEM) and checks leaf expiry (ParseCertificate → certNotAfter, used to gate TLS config refresh); test side parses CA cert/PKCS1 key and PEM-encrypts the generated key.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency (go.sum entry, no first-party import found across 496 .go files): jwt-go ships in the module graph — pulled by docker/distribution v2.7.1, whose registry token auth signs/verifies JWTs with it when origin proxies a token-auth registry. Abandoned upstream (superseded by golang-jwt/jwt; CVE-2020-26160 aud-claim bypass) — the migration note belongs on the dependency, not a call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto@v0.46.0 in the module graph (indirect require); no first-party import found — none of its primitives (ssh, bcrypt, acme, pbkdf2…) are called from kraken code today; it ships because a dependency needs it. Same logical asset as LIB-a2c61150.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Indirect dependency via docker/distribution v2.7.1 (registry token auth); no first-party call site — the JWT surface is reachable only through distribution's client when origin talks to a token-auth registry. Abandoned upstream (CVE-2020-26160); replaceable by golang-jwt/jwt on the dependency's side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Indirect x/crypto dependency at v0.46.0; reachable only through other modules in the graph. Available in the shipped library; no call site found in the application.
